senses: to be or feel cold or chilly; to become cold or chilly

la:verb:algeo.html:
algeo, alsi, 2, v. n.
acc. to Fest. from ἀλγέω = to feel pain; cf. ἄλγος, algor, and algus
,
to be cold, to feel cold; cf. P. (opp. aestuare; accordingly a subjective coldness; while frigere, opp. calere, is objective, Doed. Syn. 3, 89): si algebis, tremes, Naev. ap. : erudiunt juventutem, algendo, aestuando,: sudavit et alsit,: algentis manus est calfacienda sinu,.—Poet.: algentes togae, i. e. so torn to pieces, that those who wear them must suffer from cold,.— Trop.: probitas laudatur et alget, virtue is praised, and yet freezes, i. e. is not cherished, is neglected, .—Hence, algens, P. a., in the post-Aug. per., = algidus and frigidus, cold: pruinae,: loca,; .
